his_statement:
An immediate quadratic transform ... maximal ideal containing x; regular of dimension n.

Further occurrence (C-SA13-156): Follows from [A7, Lemma 3.19 of Section 14]
statement:
For regular noetherian local R of dimension n>1, localize the blowup chart R[m/x] at a maximal ideal containing x, where x∈m minus m². The resulting ring is regular local of dimension n, centered at m. Localization at an arbitrary nonmaximal point would not preserve dimension n.

Further occurrence (C-SA13-156): If (R,m) is a regular local ring with regular parameters x1,…,xn, then R[m/x1] is a regular blowup chart; modulo x1 it is the polynomial ring κ(m)[x2/x1,…,xn/x1]. For S=R[x2/x1,...,xn/x1], S/x1S is canonically the polynomial ring over κ(m) in n−1 residue variables. A maximal localization containing x1 is regular local of dimensionn, centered on m, with finite residue extension; x1 belongs to a regular system of parameters.

modern_statement: A presheaf on X-schemes is a big-Zariski sheaf iff its restriction to the open subsets of every object is an ordinary sheaf.
literature_fate: This is the sheaf axiom applied to the defining covering families, not a separate deep theorem. SGA4VII supplies the published scheme-site framework.

title: Jacobson closed-point topology
modern_statement: For a Jacobson scheme, the map from opens of X to opens of its closed-point subspace is bijective; hence their topoi of ordinary sheaves are equivalent.
literature_fate: The Jacobson hypothesis makes every nonempty locally closed subset contain a point closed in X. Stacks5.18.1 and5.18.7 verify the exact open-lattice comparison. Equality of the open locales gives equivalence of their sheaf topoi; it does not give a bijection of their original point sets.

title: Central quotient of inertia
modern_statement: For an open normal subgroup I′ of inertia I, let P′=ker(I′→I′_t). Then P′ is characteristic in I′, and 1→I′_t→I/P′→I/I′→1 is a central extension. This asserts centrality inside inertia, not centrality under all of G_K.
literature_fate: The canonical tame character is equivariant; inertia has trivial cyclotomic action, so conjugation by I on I′_t is trivial. This gives the manuscript corollary. Centrality does not imply splitting: for K=C((t)) and I′=mI, the resulting extension of Z/m by mZhat has no group section.

title: Weil-group compatibility and weights
modern_statement: For finite residue field, ask for rational ℓ-independent individual-degree Weil traces and integral weights0≤w≤2i for geometric Frobenius lifts; distinguish this from the weight–monodromy filtration conjecture.
literature_fate: Illusie1994 §3 formulates the weight–monodromy problem. This specific subcase does not settle the general manuscript question.

title: Approximation of a trait by regular pairs

title: Abelian schemes with virtually solvable geometric Tate action

literature_fate: The manuscript invokes Grothendieck1966 Proposition4.4 and extends its argument. The primary comparison is therefore partial: geometric semisimplicity is verified, while the exact radicial constant-part descent and the scope of this adaptation still require proposition-level collation. ClassC records that specific incomplete identification; it is not a declaration that the correctly formulated modern abelian-scheme theorem is open.

title: Potentially solvable Tate image implies CM
modern_statement: For an abelian variety over a number field, virtually solvableℓ-adic Galois image implies CM after finite extension. The same geometric property over a characteristic-zero finitely generated field requires reduction to the constant part.
literature_fate: Established for number fields by Faltings semisimplicity and the endomorphism theorem (1983, §1(a),(b)): after finite extension, a connected solvable reductive image is a torus, and its commutant contains a commutative semisimple algebra of dimension2dimA. The CM criterion then applies. Faltings’s original paper and its statements were opened; publication October1983, no first-circulation date asserted. The characteristic-zero function-field version also needs the constant-part reduction.

title: Potential good reduction does not forcep-adic inertia semisimplicity
modern_statement: Whenℓ equals residue characteristicp, potential good reduction does not imply thatV_p(A)|I is semisimple. An ordinary good-reduction elliptic lift with non-torsion Serre–Tate extension parameter gives a nonsplit extension on inertia.
literature_fate: Katz’s Serre–Tate local moduli§2 produces good-reduction deformations with nontrivial extension parameter. Brinon–Conrad2009§8.3 analyzes nonsplit crystalline extensions; finite-flat/crystalline good reduction is not semisimplicity. Thus the parenthetical converse needs deletion/restriction, pending ink inspection.

reconstruction: A concrete trait counterexample is R=W(overline F_5), K=Frac(R). Choose an ordinary elliptic curve over overline F_5 and its Serre–Tate lift with parameter q=1+5. Katz2.1 gives the connected–étale p-divisible extension. Its rational Tate extension 0→Q5(1)→V5(E)→Q5→0 is the nonzero Kummer class of q. The 5-adic logarithm has valuation1, so q cannot become infinitely5-divisible in K; no power of its Kummer class vanishes. Since the residue field is algebraically closed, G_K=I. Thus the good-reduction representation is not semisimple on inertia. Passage from compatible Artin lifts to the elliptic scheme uses the usual algebraization of polarized abelian deformations.

statement: Let f:G→H be a homomorphism of semiabelian varieties over a field k. The filtration by the maximal torus and abelian quotient is strict in the category up to isogeny. For ell invertible in k, f is an isogeny exactly when V_ell(f) is an isomorphism on geometric rational Tate modules.
computation: review.md §Semiabelian filtration: direct argument; no numerical computation.
fate: The semiabelian/weight formalism is explicit in Deligne Hodge III10.1.3–10.1.10 (documented preprint January1972, publication1974). A direct proof uses absence of homomorphisms from an abelian variety to a torus and the exact Tate sequence; integral strictness is not inferred. No proof of the Tate isogeny conjecture is involved: the map f already exists.

statement: For a morphism f:G→H in an abelian sheaf category, K=ker f satisfies K[n]=ker(G[n]→H[n]). If G[n], H[n] are finite étale group schemes over the same base, this kernel is finite étale. The additional specialization inclusion on the leaf has no recoverable complete base hypotheses.
computation: review.md §Kernel identity; separate unresolved specialization assertion is C-SA13-310.
fate: The kernel identity is a formal intersection of two kernels and is independently proved here. Finite étale kernels follow by étale local constant finite groups. SGA7 IX concerns the specialization context, but the isolated eta/s-subscript assertion is not uniquely identified.

statement: Proposed counterexample: deform E×F, with E ordinary elliptic and F nonordinary elliptic in characteristic p, through abelian schemes so the generic abelian surface is geometrically simple. Then the special ordinary elliptic factor cannot lift as a positive-dimensional proper abelian subvariety of the generic fibre.
computation: No numerical computation is required; see the proof analysis in review.md.
fate: The implication from a generically simple family is valid; the page does not construct that family or specify the intended lifting category. Searches of the SGA7 IX and abelian-deformation literature did not certify the exact family here. This does not rule out a formal or p-divisible subgroup lift, and is not recorded as a completed refutation of a recovered published theorem.

statement: In a finite filtered object with exact Cartier duality, if a pairing respects opposite filtrations and every associated graded pairing is perfect, the total pairing is perfect. This applies to finite locally free torsion group schemes once the orthogonality statements and graded identifications have been proved.
computation: review.md §Filtered perfectness; computations.py checks the block-triangular matrix illustration, not a proof for every sheaf.
fate: The implication is an elementary induction on exact sequences (five lemma), independently proved here. It is not a deduction from equal ranks alone. The concrete graded factors are standard in Deligne’s1-motive and abelian duality formalism.

statement: Hasse derivative D_p extracts the coefficient of at^p in characteristic p, while the ordinary derivative kills it. fate: Hasse operators, rather than ordinary derivatives, are the characteristic-free coefficient operators. Over a Q-algebra the two closure conditions coincide. Merely saying “characteristic0” after replacing the field by an arbitrary ring does not itself justify division by factorials. The example Z[t,t²/2] shows the ordinary-derivation argument is insufficient, but is not asserted to satisfy all multivariable substitution/H axioms. The margin therefore remains a scope alarm, not a full-system counterexample.

his_statement: Th.2.1: semistable μ≥0; stable μ>0, all1-PS.
statement: For an ample G-linearized line bundle on a proper scheme over an algebraically closed field with G reductive in the source’s convention, semistability is equivalent to μ(x,λ)≥0 for every one-parameter subgroup; proper stability is equivalent to μ(x,λ)>0 for every nontrivial one-parameter subgroup. If the trivial subgroup is allowed in the strict inequality, μ=0 makes the literal statement false.

fate: False in this unrestricted noetherian generality. Orgogozo2014 XVIII_B §§2.1–2.4 constructs a regular strictly henselian dimension2 A with principal U=D(F) and H3(U,Z/ℓ)≠0. statement: Pinch a k-rational special point on each of two copies of P1_S to one point. The resulting proper flat family has pure one-dimensional fibres, rectified fibre depth≥1 and isolated nonsmooth special point, but H0(Xs,Λ)=Λ→H0(X_Kbar,Λ)=Λ² is diagonal, so Φman^1 contains a nonzero copy ofΛ.

fate: The manuscript itself supplies the counterexample. The local pinching ring R[x]×_k R[y] is torsion-free over the DVR, hence flat; its generic fibre is the disjoint union. Its closed fibre is connected and has no zero-dimensional irreducible component, though an embedded nilpotent at the join explains why it is not a relative lci. The displayed H^(0|1) must be H0.
